findings.namedBuyers: Two primary relationship-entry contacts are verified: SK Uddin, Show Organizer and CanadianSME Editor & Publisher; and Maheen Bari, CanadianSME Client Manager and named member of the Show 2027 team. SK is relevant for organizer-level routing; Maheen for client/event relationship coordination. Additional published Show contacts are Kripa Anand and Raoof Uddin Shaik; the Show page does not assign them procurement roles. None is verified as the hotel contract signatory, housing buyer or room-block owner.
findings.futureEdition: Confirmed upcoming edition: May 21, 2027, a one-day event in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. Official event copy gives the activity date, independently matched by the organizer’s Eventbrite listing (8 a.m.–6 p.m.). Both start and end date are May 21, not a press-release publication date. This falls within the requested horizon. No officially announced 2028 edition was located; do not extrapolate a 2028 date.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specification: realistic only as a partial lodging partner for visiting speakers, exhibitors, organizers, executives or delegates, potentially with small side meetings. The 2027 organizer anticipates around 3,000 attendees and 100+ exhibitors; those are not overnight guests. A 157-room hotel cannot house the whole event and its approximately 240-theatre largest room cannot replace the main Show venue. Harbourfront proximity to MTCC supports a short-stay city-hotel proposition, not a resort retreat or evidenced relocation/extended-stay programme. A 15–109 peak-room proposal would be a hotel-side qualification range only, not published event demand. Do not promise catering or a reception until restaurant/lounge and service capability are verified.
findings.venueCommitments: Published 2027 venue: Metro Toronto Convention Centre, North Building, Level 100, 255 Front Street West, Toronto, Ontario M5V 2W6, Canada. This is Toronto proper, downtown/MTCC territory, not the organizer’s Mississauga office. It is a convention centre, not a competing hotel. Organizer announcement establishes the published venue; no signed 2027 venue contract was inspected.
findings.historicalRotation: Evidence covers June 16, 2023; June 24, 2024; May 29, 2025; and May 22, 2026, all at MTCC in Toronto. The 2023 archive specifically retains Conference Hall 107 (Constitutional Hall), but its site-wide header has rolled forward to 2026; do not read that header as a 2023 date. The 2024–2026 sources specify North Building, Level 100. These consecutive editions establish recurrence and destination retention, not rotation among cities or an invariant annual date. Keep the separate Small Business Summit and awards programmes out of this timeline.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Unknown/unconfirmed. No edition-specific host hotel, named accommodation hotel, room block, housing bureau, booking code, room-night allocation or open hotel RFP was verified. The official venue page says: “A convenient indoor tunnel connects event-goers to two hotels, Union Station and the UP Express”; neither hotel is named there and the statement is generic venue-access information, not a housing commitment. The exhibitor FAQ asks “Are there hotel partnerships or special rates?” but the retrieved page publishes no answer. Hotels listed as edition-specific accommodation: none verified. Do not infer either open sourcing or committed lodging from this silence.
findings.organizationStructure: CanadianSME Small Business Magazine produces the Show. The official About page describes Cmarketing Inc. as “a marketing agency and business management boutique” that publishes the magazine; 2026 exhibitor terms name Cmarketing Inc. as organizer. The 2027 contact page gives Cmarketing Inc.’s Mississauga head office. Classify this as a publisher/marketing-agency-led commercial business event, not an association congress. No separate appointed PCO, DMC or housing bureau was identified. Do not treat MTCC as the event owner.
findings.competitiveLimitations: The core event is already assigned publicly to MTCC, so do not pitch replacement main-show meeting space. The venue advertises tunnel access to two unnamed hotels, a potential convenience advantage over an off-site hotel; this is not evidence of contracted incumbents. No sourced sell-out, shortage, overflow requirement or exclusive lodging arrangement was found. The free, single-day format limits confidence in overnight conversion; this is a commercial inference, not a published room-demand figure.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Contact SK Uddin and Maheen Bari jointly, referencing May 21, 2027 at MTCC. Ask who manages visiting-speaker, staff and exhibitor lodging; whether any hotels/housing vendor are contracted; whether hotel partnerships or special rates exist; and for out-of-town headcount, arrival/departure dates, peak rooms, room nights, budget and procurement timing. Only after those answers, offer a non-exclusive short-stay lodging proposal sized to actual demand and available inventory, with optional small meetings subject to hotel service verification. If 2027 is closed, request the next planning review and hotel-partner criteria without asserting an announced 2028 edition.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: For the 2027 edition, organizer contact is accessible and exhibiting/sponsorship channels are published, but lodging procurement accessibility remains unconfirmed. MTCC venue confirmation does not establish hotel sourcing closure. Treat this as a qualification conversation, not an open room-block lead; do not buy a booth merely to seek rooms without a demand discussion.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: the documented return to Toronto/MTCC across several editions makes a repeat organizer lodging relationship more plausible than bidding for a destination rotation. Seek a small non-exclusive speaker/exhibitor accommodation arrangement first, then future-cycle inclusion if travel demand is established. No 2028 activity date, venue, lodging tender or future inventory is confirmed; any later-cycle capture strategy is prospective only.
